summary: The correspondence workflow stores separate proposals, conditional analyses and reviewer decisions against completed source-bound investigations. Review the concrete implementation with role, staleness, rejection, archive and release-block tests before frozen-source replay.
findings: Owner-only proposals and analyses use server-configured Java. Meaning reviewers must be distinct from the investigation owner; a body-supplied approval or executable is rejected.
A proposal binds exact source, both reading commitments, final search-state hash and report hash. Recheck source status and concurrent rejection after compilation before saving an analysis.
Analysis is permitted as an explicit unreviewed hypothesis, but all results remain CONDITIONAL_ANALYSIS. Reviewer acceptance does not resolve source meaning or grant release.
Later rejection is appended and visible with earlier analysis. New analyses are blocked on a rejected proposal. Existing search reports, issues and candidates are not rewritten.
Archive portability and current source invalidation are tested. The local identity registry is not proof of actual human qualifications or independence.
Use the trusted fixed supervisor for TestClient tests because earlier sandboxed supervisor stalls were not explained. No live provider calls are planned.
